lawyer:
Nizamul Hoque Nasim, Advocate------For the Petitioner. 
Shahabuddin Ahmad, Deputy Attorney-General------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Modhumala  ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Director, Housing & Building Research Institute & others  ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: The respondent No. 1, Housing and Building Research Institute in its Affidavit-in-opposition contended amongst others, that the lands in question is not a khas land of the Government but a project land acquired for Housing and Building Research Institute and that the possession of the acquired land was delivered to the authority in due course and that the use of the acquired land was being done phase by phase and accordingly, some unutilised land were left out for some time on which the petitioner and some others illegally trespassed into and are occupying the same illegally and forcibly and that the said land is now required for the purpose of completion of the project of the respondent No. 1 and hence eviction process was initiated and that too following the provision of law for eviction ie, section 5 of the Ordinance XXIV of 1970, and accordingly, 7 (seven) days notice was given for vacating the basti but basti people did not respond and that the notice for eviction was given on 26-12- 93 fixing 5-1-94 as date for eviction and that the Housing and Building Research Institute is a statutory body and is a project for the benefit of the citizens of the country and that petitioner being a trespasser has no locus standi to take shelter of the writ jurisdiction and in view of the provisions of Act 32 of 1989 the interim order of status quo need be vacated.
